validator: draft 1 passes (no problems, soft or warnings); the faults below are the critic's.
keep: The idea is named up front in two plain sentences (a rate added up over time gives the total; bars do it, the reverse rule gets it in one subtraction), built from what Dan has: a steady rate times a time [7], an amp as a coulomb each second (lesson 5) and the reverse rule q = t³ + c (lesson 7).

One fully worked example with real numbers from the rule: i = 3t² from 0 s to 2 s, bars at their starts 0, 0.75, 3, 6.75 A giving 5.25 C, then 6.56 C at 8 bars and 7.88 C at 100, settling on 8 C = (8 + c) − (0 + c), with the c cancelling [5]. All checked by computing the sums: 5.25, 6.5625, 7.8804; mid-height 7.875.

The causal step is there: each thin bar is the rate of growth times a short time, so it is nearly the rise of q across that bar, and the rises join end to end into F(b) − F(a) [2]; bars approximate, the rule is exact [1].

Every misconception the brief names for lesson 8 has a DO screen with its own slip: height read as the amount (step 2, 5 m), a bar's area read as a current (step 4, 1.5 A), F(a) not taken away (steps 6 and 11), the ends put into the rate instead of F (steps 6 and 11), all area counted plus (steps 10 and 12) and start minus end (step 12). The area-or-accumulation finding is taught from [8], in its own qualifiers ('did not necessarily').

Twelve screens alternate SHOW (1, 3, 5, 7, 9) and DO (2, 4, 6, 8, 10), ending on two mixed puzzles (11, 12). Hand-checked: 12; 30, 5, 11; 1.5, 3.5; 7, 8, 9; 70, 35, 150, 72; 4, 1, 3; 0, 9, 4.5; 24, 28, 6; 5, 13, −5; practice 15 − 7 = 8 and 4 × 2 = 8; lesson 7's capacitor 3 + 8 = 11 C.
fix: Faithful to the source: [7] is about a constant velocity, but the draft hangs it on 'when a rate holds steady'. Cite it on the speed sentence and give the general step (any steady rate times its time) as reasoning of the lesson's own.
False absolute: 'it is how you add up a graph you have only as readings' says the mid-ordinate rule is the way. Say it is one way; other strip rules exist.
Interactive brief shows only the effect (the total settling), not its cause. Name the slivers between the bars and the curve shrinking as the total settles.
Recommended shape, the misconception shown failing: the minus is stated but the slip is not shown going wrong. Show counting the 1 C back as plus giving 5 C, more than ever arrived.

Causal step thin for mid-height bars: say where each sliver is (the bar pokes above the curve on its left half, the curve rises above the bar on its right half) so it is plain why they nearly cancel, and why a straight line makes them match exactly.
Reading order: paragraph 3 carries the rule, its why, the notation and the mid-ordinate rule. Move the mid-height bars to the end of the bars paragraph, where they belong.
Causal gap: '∫₀⁴ t dt = 0.5 × 16 − 0' skips where 0.5t² comes from; name it as the reverse rule's answer for t.
ignores claims the bars are drawn with gaps between them; at 100 bars across 340 px that cannot be promised by the brief. Drop it.
Continuity: the analogy uses the kWh meter from lesson 1 with the same mapping (reading = the amount, power = the rate); say so by name, and soften 'moment by moment' to 'as it happens'.
verdict: Rewrite as draft 2 with these nine fixes; nothing else needs to change.
